cells.tense: You are here in the open room, in contact, and still your own person.
cells.ask: Say one true sentence about what came down, in front of someone who watched it happen. Keep your own side of it while you talk. Then stop and let the quiet sit a minute.
cells.core:
You're in a clearing and you're not alone in it. Whatever frame came down, you can feel it wasn't built to hold, and you kept your footing when it went. You're with the people around you and you keep your own edges, which is the part most people can't manage. It costs you something and you pay it without complaint.

Holding without forcing is what keeps this. Not more feeling — endurance, the plain kind. Something steady underneath while others lean on it, and no grabbing for a new frame to fill the space the old one left. That's what this balance is free to feed next, and it is optional. Keep it up and the clearing stays workable for the people in it.

cells.tense: You are already past the clearing, bracing for ground that has not moved yet.
cells.ask: Hand back one thing today that belongs to someone else, and say out loud it's theirs. Then watch your hands for the rest of the day and put down anything you picked up unasked.
cells.core:
You're standing where the frames came down with other people, and you're running ahead of it. Someone's ground shifts and yours goes with them — the line between their end and yours has loosened, and their falling turns into yours to carry. You take the measure of a need before it's spoken, and the clearing fills with weight that hasn't arrived here.

What fits is an ending, done clean. Give one thing back that was theirs from the start and name it as theirs. Letting something finish is a real act and it doesn't need to be loud. Then the clearing holds only what's here — not the futures you're bracing against, not loads you took on to stop somebody else from going down.

cells.tense: You were in a room where things came down, and you are still standing out at the door.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about how the last few weeks have been for you, to someone you see often. Then stop and let them answer before anything else gets said.
cells.core:
Something came down close to you and you didn't step in. You can see the cleared space from the doorway and you're keeping your distance, holding exchanges at arm's length where the shape of another person's stuff might reach you. Ties stay thin because you stop at the surface, and that's a move you keep making without quite choosing it.

It comes back through small adjustments, not one big feeling. Toward one person, say one real thing and let it land. Then wait. Nothing here requires energy you don't have right now — just open a single line and let a little through. The ground under you holds, and it held before whatever came down came down.

cells.tense: The pen is down and the writing is still going on, right now, in this room.
cells.ask: Write down one thing done for someone lately that got filed under logistics. Then read it back and add: this is care, on purpose. Keep the paper.
cells.core:
The connecting is running. People lean in, something in the room settles when you're in it, and the account you give is that you were just being sensible. Standing in the same room, another person would call you the one holding it together. The feeling you report as missing is the thing you're most consistently doing.

What brings it back isn't more feeling. It's seeing the shape underneath — one act, named plainly as care, on purpose, once. The clearing in front of you is made of what already happened, not what has to be managed next. Name one piece of it as yours and the rest stops being something carried without knowing why it's heavy.
